subject: physics
title: Atomic number, mass number and isotopes
key_idea: The **atomic number** is the number of protons and identifies the element. The **mass number** is protons plus neutrons. **Isotopes** are atoms of the same element with the same number of protons but a different number of neutrons.

blocks.text: Two numbers describe the nucleus of an atom. This section covers what they mean and how to find the number of neutrons.

items.meaning: The number of protons in an atom. Every atom of an element has the same atomic number.
The total number of protons and neutrons in an atom.

items: In a neutral atom the number of electrons equals the number of protons.
The atomic number fixes the charge of the nucleus, so it fixes the element.
A nucleus is written with the mass number at the top and the atomic number at the bottom, for example ²³⁸₉₂U.
²³⁸₉₂U means mass number 238 and atomic number 92. It has 92 protons.

blocks.label: Number of neutrons
blocks.formula: number of neutrons = mass number - atomic number
where: Mass number is the number of protons plus neutrons.
Atomic number is the number of protons.

items.text: For ²³⁸₉₂U the mass number is 238 and the atomic number is 92.
Neutrons = 146. There are 92 protons and 92 electrons.

diagram.question: A uranium nucleus has atomic number 92 and mass number {A}. Calculate the number of neutrons in the nucleus.

items: Atomic number is the number of protons. Mass number is protons plus neutrons.
A neutral atom has equal numbers of protons and electrons.

blocks.text: Atoms of one element are not all identical. They can differ in the number of neutrons.

items.meaning: Atoms of the same element with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.

items: Isotopes have the same atomic number but different mass numbers.
The nucleus of each element has a characteristic positive charge, so isotopes of an element have the same charge.
Isotopes differ in mass because of their neutrons.
Carbon-12 has 6 protons and 6 neutrons. Carbon-14 has 6 protons and 8 neutrons.
Isotopes of one element have the same number of electrons, so they react in the same way.

blocks.text: Move the slider to change the number of neutrons in a carbon atom. The protons and electrons stay the same.

diagram.alt: Change the number of neutrons in a carbon nucleus and see the mass number.

items: Isotopes have the same number of protons and a different number of neutrons.
Isotopes have the same atomic number and a different mass number.

blocks.text: An atom has no overall charge. It becomes an ion when it gains or loses electrons.

items: An atom that loses one or more outer electrons becomes a positive ion.
The number of protons does not change, so there are now more protons than electrons.
The nucleus is unchanged, so the element stays the same.
Losing an electron makes a positive ion.
Only the electrons change. The nucleus stays the same.

checks.q: A gold atom is written ¹⁹⁷₇₉Au. How many protons, neutrons and electrons does it have?
State what is the same and what is different in two isotopes of an element.
checks.a: They have the same number of protons (the same atomic number). They have a different number of neutrons (a different mass number).

checks.q: What happens to an atom when it becomes a positive ion?
checks.a: It loses one or more outer electrons.

exam_phrases: (atoms of an element with) the same number of protons
but a different number of neutrons
positive charge is provided by protons
the atom becomes a positive ion

mistakes.wrong: Isotopes have the same number of protons and neutrons.
mistakes.right: This is not accepted. Isotopes have the same number of protons and a different number of neutrons.

mistakes.wrong: All atoms of an element have the same positive charge because they have the same number of protons and neutrons.
mistakes.right: Do not accept protons and neutrons together. The positive charge is provided by protons, and every atom of the element has the same number of them.

mistakes.wrong: Isotopes of an element have a different number of electrons.
mistakes.right: Reference to electrons is ignored. The difference is the number of neutrons.

worked_example.question:
Americium-241 (²⁴¹₉₅Am) is an isotope of americium.

Isotope A has mass number 243 and atomic number 95.
Isotope B has mass number 243 and atomic number 94.
Isotope C has mass number 242 and atomic number 95.

Which of these isotopes is not an isotope of americium?

Give a reason for your answer.
answer_points: Americium has an atomic number of 95, and B has an atomic number of 94.
worked_example.tip: The reason scores only if B is chosen. Proton number is accepted for atomic number.

mistakes.wrong: A similarity between fluorine-19 and a radioactive isotope of fluorine is the same number of neutrons.
mistakes.right: The neutrons are what differ. The marks are for the same number of protons (the same atomic number) and a different number of neutrons (a different mass number).

mistakes.wrong: Carbon-13 has 6 neutrons and carbon-14 has 8 neutrons.
mistakes.right: Both numbers in a column must be correct for the mark. Carbon-13 has 13 - 6 = 7 neutrons.

worked_example.question:
Carbon-13 and carbon-14 are isotopes of carbon.

Nuclei of carbon-13 and carbon-14 can be represented by the symbols ¹³₆C and ¹⁴₆C.

Complete a table for an atom of carbon-13 and an atom of carbon-14 giving the number of neutrons in the nucleus and the number of electrons in orbit around the nucleus.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each column, so both numbers in the column must be right.

mistakes.wrong: Carbon-14 and carbon-12 have the same number of neutrons.
mistakes.right: This is not allowed. They have the same number of protons and a different number of neutrons.

mistakes.wrong: Carbon-14 and carbon-12 have a different number of protons.
mistakes.right: This is not allowed. Carbon-14 and carbon-12 both have 6 protons.

mistakes.wrong: The two isotopes have a different number of protons and neutrons.
mistakes.right: This is unclear and not allowed. Name the particle that changes: it is only the neutrons.

worked_example.question:
The carbon-14 atom has 6 protons and 8 neutrons in its nucleus.

Carbon-12 is a different isotope of carbon.

State one similarity and one difference between an atom of carbon-14 and an atom of carbon-12.
answer_points: Similarity: the same number of protons (the same number of electrons or the same atomic number is also allowed).
Difference: a different number of neutrons (a different mass number is also allowed).
worked_example.tip: Carbon-12 has 6 protons and 6 neutrons. Say which particle is the same and which is different.
